rounds.text: Raj Packaging Industries Ltd is experiencing a powerful operational turnaround that the market has not yet fully priced in, trading at an attractive P/E of 14x and P/B of 1.11x, both well below their respective sector benchmarks of 22.48x and 2.44x [E1, E2, E6, E7]. Recent results demonstrate dramatic momentum, highlighted by 20% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a staggering 248% compounded profit growth over the same period, alongside a massive positive divergence where profit growth exceeds 1-year price growth by 276% [E17, E21, E47]. Profitability is structurally improving as operating margins expanded to 6% in the TTM from -2% three years prior, reaching 9% in the quarter ending June 2026 [E30, E31]. This earnings surge is exceptionally high-quality, backed by a cash conversion ratio of 4.69x yielding Rs 1.64 Cr in pure operating and free cash flow for March 2026, which has enabled the company to actively reduce its borrowings from Rs 4.98 Cr to Rs 3.72 Cr and lower its debt-to-equity to a conservative 0.29x [E34, E35, E36, E37, E38, E49]. Insider confidence is notably strengthening as well, with promoters increasing their stake by 3.69 percentage points from 32.66% in December 2023 to 36.35% by September 2026, all operating against a supportive Capital Goods macro tailwind score of +0.67 [E40, E63]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E16, E18, E19, E24, E25, E43, E44, E54].

The valuation is detached from fundamentals, with a discounted cash flow model showing intrinsic value at Rs 24 per share against a market price of Rs 31.3, translating to a negative margin of safety of 30.0% [E43, E44]. Long-term top-line erosion remains severe, evidenced by compounded sales growth of -2% over 10 years, -4% over 5 years, and -11% over 3 years [E14, E15, E16]. Profitability metrics are chronically depressed, highlighted by a 10-year median return on equity of 3% that drops to -1% over 5 years and -5% over 3 years [E26, E27, E28], alongside a low current ROE of 2.7% and ROCE of 5.0% [E12, E13]. Furthermore, promoter holding sits low at 36.4%, and the dividend yield is completely absent at 0.00% [E4, E53]. Conceded: the company has expanded its operating margin over the last four years and achieved a TTM operating cash flow of Rs 1.64 Cr with strong cash conversion [E30, E32, E34, E35].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model suggests an intrinsic value of Rs 24, resulting in a negative margin of safety [E43, E44], and long-term historical sales growth over 10, 5, and 3 years is negative [E14, E15, E16]. Conceded: the 10-year median ROE is 3%, dropping to -1% and -5% over shorter periods [E26, E27, E28], current ROE and ROCE remain low [E12, E13], promoter holding is 36.4% [E53], and the dividend yield is absent at 0.00% [E4]. However, focusing solely on historical figures ignores an explosive operational inflection where TTM sales growth reached 20% [E17] and TTM profit growth surged by 248% [E21], accompanied by recent quarterly net profit soaring 558% year-over-year [E58]. This turnaround is further validated by a sector tailwind score of +0.67 in Capital Goods [E63, E65], an operating margin expanding to 6% in TTM and 9% in the latest quarter [E30, E31], and pristine cash conversion of 4.69x generating Rs 1.64 Cr in free cash flow alongside ongoing debt reduction [E34, E36, E38, E49].

Conceded: TTM sales grew 20% [E17] and TTM profit surged 248% [E21], with quarterly net profit up 558% year-over-year [E58] alongside an operating margin of 9% in June 2026 [E31] and debt reduction [E49]. However, relying on these explosive short-term metrics ignores the deeply entrenched structural decline characterized by negative compounded sales growth over 10, 5, and 3 years [E14, E15, E16]. Conceded: the capital goods sector carries a tailwind score of +0.67 [E63, E65], and the company generated Rs 1.64 Cr in free cash flow with strong cash conversion [E34, E36]. Yet, this operational improvement fails to justify a stock price of Rs 31.3 when the discounted cash flow model places intrinsic value at Rs 24, leaving an unsupportable margin of safety of -30% [E43, E44]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already bakes in ongoing growth expectations that far exceed the baseline assumptions [E45], while the broader fundamental reality remains anchored by chronic low returns on equity of 2.7% [E13] and poor long-term historical profit growth [E18, E19]. Finally, low promoter holding at 36.4% [E53] and a complete absence of dividend yield at 0.00% [E4] offer no cushion for investors paying a premium over the DCF valuation.
